body: Colorado's chatbot rulemaking timeline (SB 24-205 and related proposed rulemaking) moves through a phased structure: proposed rules → public comment → final adoption → phased enforcement. The Council of AI does not claim to 'approve' or 'certify' any chatbot deployment as compliant; instead it produces verified measurement credentials of monitored containment for the AI systems involved, enabling a Colorado regulator or a UK-prime deployer to reference independently measured evidence during a rulemaking comment or an OSCAL-structured audit. The measurement board covers synthetic-content provenance (Article 50(2) alignment), detection (det axis, weakest at 0.000 consistent with format/transport failure — not capability deficit), care (care axis, spread ~0.879→0.035 identified), denial, and governance. Each observation binds to a fixed, Ed25519-signed manifest. The fix candidate for the det gap (0.000 weakest model, 33/33 unparsed) is an adapter-level regex fallback extracting the answer token from reasoning blocks — a transport fix, not a capability claim. No kinetic-targeting, personal-surveillance, or 'AUKUS partnership' / 'DAIC certified' claims; DEFONEOS-SEAL requires 33-agent BFT council vote (quorum 23/33); no defonos.io domain reference.
